what: Santa Maria Hostel provides residential and outpatient substance use treatment for women, including pregnant and parenting women.
Its Houston programs combine counseling, recovery support, childcare, housing assistance and career development.
The deep review uses reported treatment/support activity as a conditional envelope and includes signed health and net household resources.
strengths: Current services address childcare and housing barriers alongside substance use treatment.
The new 2025 impact report separates treatment/support, prevention and unique clinic patients.
Local MIRRORS follow-up and randomized external case-management evidence support recovery and work mechanisms without supplying causal Houston utility or dollar earnings.
reservations: The 1,404 treatment/detox/support women are not verified unique completed treatments, and post-closure throughput remains unknown.
Recovery utility and net earnings effects are unsupported local priors, not measured causal effects.
Whole-recipient costs include prevention, family services and Austin, while this numerator covers a narrow Houston women’s channel.

sections.what: Santa Maria Hostel provides residential and outpatient substance use treatment for women, including pregnant and parenting women. Its Houston programs combine counseling, recovery support, childcare, housing assistance and career development. The deep review uses reported treatment/support activity as a conditional envelope and includes signed health and net household resources.
sections.monitoring: The September 2026 download is titled 2025 Annual Report and records 1,404 women receiving treatment, detox and supportive services, not unique completed care. Its 12,099 mixed family total and 599 unique I-Care patients are different populations, not added beneficiaries. The June 2025 notice projects residential/outpatient capacity at 60% after closures; other programs and Austin continue. Request dated unique completed treatment episodes and unique women, relapse and health outcomes, retained disposable earnings, current Houston share and a post-closure budget.
sections.qualitative: Local MIRRORS research follows 215 pregnant/postpartum women from intake to discharge and six months post-intake, without an untreated control. Improvements are descriptive rather than incremental causal recovery or earnings. A randomized New Jersey TANF intensive-case-management trial supports abstinence and work mechanisms versus screening/referral, but differs from Santa Maria residential care and measures neither Houston QALYs nor net dollar earnings. Current services combine childcare and career support; intensive curricula occupy 30 hours/week, supportive groups at least 10 hours/week. Foregone time, taxes, withdrawn benefits, travel and childcare may offset gains. No retail service values, maternal mortality or ordinary survivor earnings are automatically counted.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $54.45M per better life: 4.633930 health QALYs and -1.570142 signed income equivalents. The original $110.99M becomes $178.37M when only all-exposure burden accounting is corrected at the original 300-person cohort; using the reported 2025 category envelope then gives $54.45M. These are scope/accounting revisions, not measured improvement in whole-portfolio effectiveness. Full recognized FY2025 cost remains $16,681,490. N=1,404 is the reported mixed treatment/detox/support category, unique=.7 a household-mapping judgment, giving 982.8 exposed proxies. Additionality .4 and clinical completion .5 yield 196.56 responders. Original .05 utility for half a year, quarter-year delay and Houston share .95 remain judgments, especially given 15 counties and Austin. A .6 capacity-flow sensitivity is a hypothesis, not a blanket observed multiplier. A quarter of incremental households receives $1,000 one-year disposable resources after taxes, benefit withdrawal and recurring work costs; positive components alone receive .5 overlap. Each exposed household incurs full $100 access burden even without additional recovery. One joint household log uses $15,000 positive baseline consumption; clinical null retains financial exposures and burden. Central zero harm and external losses are unknown-neutral placeholders, tested with full negative harm, lost-work/opportunity cost, payer/provider losses and displaced-worker stresses. Public payer incidence allocates Houston recipients once then uses payer edition share one. No additionality differs from no exposure. Full annual cost against only this finite Houston treatment channel omits unmeasured prevention, clinic, children, Austin and other benefits rather than assuming zero; it is not portfolio EV or verified next-gift capacity.
sections.funding: Gross recognized expenses are FY2025 $16,681,490, FY2024 $15,639,260 and FY2023 $13,307,636, including direct event costs netted from revenue. Schedule D removed expense amounts match these event addbacks; no additional donated-service amount is identified. The series covers the entire recipient, not only Houston residential care. The organization announced a $15 million five-year public funding reduction; this does not prove a particular donation restores a bed or replaces that funding dollar-for-dollar. Current fundraising does not establish a donation restores a particular bed; the five-year funding loss is not an annual expense or a verified replacement ratio. Financial originals were reviewed in the accepted October 5 audit; fresh October 6 IRS retrieval was blocked, so these figures are reused, not claimed newly reverified.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: The 2025 reported treatment/detox/support envelope spans 15 Texas counties and the whole recipient. Houston share .95 is a retained judgment, not an observed Houston-only cohort; Austin and other non-MSA participants remain uncertain and geography sensitivity applies.
model.formula: exposed=N*unique; incremental=exposed*b; clinical=incremental*completion; health=(clinical*q*discounted finite years - exposed*harm)*g; successes=incremental*success; disjoint household joint signed logs with full exposed costs; locally allocated distinct payer losses once; price=10*C/(health+income equivalent)
model.counterfactual: Alternative charity/public care, recovery supports, insurance eligibility, household behavior and funding replacement; additional response remains a prior.
model.attribution: Benefit additionality is separate from full service exposure burden; current capacity flow is a sensitivity, not observed annual outcomes.
model.uncertainty: Unique households, Houston share, causal utility, completion, persistence, disposable resources, harms, payer losses and marginal capacity remain unresolved hypotheses.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2025 report: 1,404 women receiving treatment/detox/support, not unique completed care. Mixed continuum and clinic populations kept separate.
